title: Notes on the analytical engine
body: A machine that weaves algebraic patterns the way a loom weaves flowers and leaves.

title: On computable numbers
body: A definite method for deciding whether a number can be written down by a machine.

title: The first compiler
body: Nobody believed a computer could understand English, so the compiler was written anyway.

title: Universality, again
body: One machine that can imitate every other one, given the right description on its tape.

title: Go to statement considered harmful
body: The quality of programmers is a decreasing function of the density of go to statements.

title: A behavioural notion of subtyping
body: If it looks like the supertype and behaves like it, the program cannot tell the difference.

title: Reflections on trusting trust
body: You cannot trust code you did not totally create yourself. Not even the compiler.

title: Software engineering, the term
body: The guidance software needed a name to be taken as seriously as the hardware around it.

title: Checking the trajectory by hand
body: The numbers came out of the machine, and then somebody had to agree with them.

title: The machine has no pretensions
body: It can do whatever we know how to order it to perform, and nothing beyond that.
